sources.title: CVE-2020-13945: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: In Apache APISIX, the user enabled the Admin API and deleted the Admin API access IP restriction rules. Eventually, the default token is allowed to access APISIX management data. This affects versions 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2020-13945 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2021-33190: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: In Apache APISIX Dashboard version 2.6, we changed the default value of listen host to 0.0.0.0 in order to facilitate users to configure external network access. In the IP allowed list restriction, a risky function was used for the IP acquisition, which made it possible to bypass the network limit. At the same time, the default account and password are fixed.Ultimately these factors lead to the issue of security risks. This issue is fixed in APISIX Dashboard 2.6.1
supports: NVD lists CVE-2021-33190 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

sources.title: CVE-2021-43557: NVD vulnerability record
sources.snippet: The uri-block plugin in Apache APISIX before 2.10.2 uses $request_uri without verification. The $request_uri is the full original request URI without normalization. This makes it possible to construct a URI to bypass the block list on some occasions. For instance, when the block list contains "^/internal/", a URI like `//internal/` can be used to bypass it. Some other plugins also have the same issue. And it may affect the developer's custom plugin.
supports: NVD lists CVE-2021-43557 as a research lead; product identity, version applicability, and exploitation remain unverified.

The exact schema and behavior depend on the APISIX release, so verify the documentation for the version you run. The plugin details below were verified against APISIX 3.18.0. ai-proxy-multi supports multiple configured model instances with documented load-balancing and fallback behavior. In APISIX 3.18.0, when a failed upstream is retried, the plugin records that instance’s error body in the error log. Treat those logs as potentially sensitive and review their access, export, and retention before enabling fallback. General authentication, request transformation, traffic control, and logging plugins can be composed with these features. In APISIX 3.18.0, ai-proxy forwards client headers other than Host, Content-Length, and Accept-Encoding unless they are removed or overwritten.
